newsitem.title: ALBANIA: European assessment team arrives in Albania.
newsitem.headline: European assessment team arrives in Albania.

text.p: A high-level European assessment team arrived in Albania on Monday for talks on how to help the new broad-based government end the anarchy in the Balkan state, witnesses said.

The 11-strong team, led by Dutch roving ambassador Jan de Marchant et d'Ansembourg, flew into Tirana by Italian military helicopter from the southern port of Brindisi after a preparatory meeting at the Foreign Ministry in Rome.
The team arrived in Tirana in two giant twin-rotored Chinook helicopters, escorted by two smaller helicopters which hovered over the landing zone at the American diplomatic compound in Tirana.

Diplomatic sources said the mission would first meet the ambassadors to Albania from the European Union and the United States before talks with Prime Minister Bashkim Fino and ministers in his national unity government.

The mission was also expected to visit the ports of Durres and Vlore, key bridgeheads in any relief aid operation, during its two-day stay. No meeting with President Sali Berisha was immediately planned, the sources said.

EU foreign ministers declined at the weekend to answer an Albanian call for military intervention. Instaed the team would pave the way for a mission by up to 150 experts to help the Albanian authorities restore security and distribute aid.
